chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Mutamatti' (pilgrim who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') does not spend the night in Mina on the Day of Sacrifice until he has visited the House.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The pilgrim who performs Hajj al-Tamattu', a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj.
key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina, the tent city near Mecca where pilgrims stay.
key_terms.يَزُورَ الْبَيْتَ: To visit the House (Kaaba), referring to the ritual of Tawaf.
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice, referring to the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim regarding spending the night in Mina on Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar underscores the obligatory nature of Tawaf al-Ziyarah for the Mutamatti' pilgrim, specifying that it must be completed before the first night in Mina. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the distinct sequence of rituals for Mutamatti' compared to Mufrid and Qarini, emphasizing the centrality of the Kaaba visit as a primary pillar of their Hajj validity.
